predecessors.name: Kingdom of the Franks
predecessors.text: the Basque valleys round Pamplona that the Franks 'in 806 took ... under their protection'

successors.name: Kingdom of Castile
successors.text: La Rioja, the Lordship of Biscay, the County of Álava, the County of Durango and part of Gipuzkoa, taken by Alfonso VI in 1076

successors.name: Kingdom of Aragon
successors.text: 'the rest of the territory', taken by Sancho Ramírez of Aragon in 1076, whose core was 'recognised by Alfonso VI as a vassal state'

rulers.name: Sancho and García of Viguera (regents for Sancho III)

ledger.x: 824: Íñigo Arista becomes ruler of Pamplona.
844: Galindo Aznárez I of Aragon becomes Íñigo's vassal.
914: Sancho takes Arnedo.
922: the vassalage ends in absorption.
922: the county of Aragon is absorbed.
923: Viguera and Nájera fall.
966: Calahorra is lost.
1015: Sancho III begins to expand into Sobrarbe.
1017: Sancho becomes protector of Castile.
1018: Ribagorza passes to Sancho III.
1025: the rival claim to Ribagorza ends.
1028: Count García Sánchez of Castile is assassinated.
1028: Sancho III occupies Castile.
1028: Sancho takes the Pisuerga and the Cea from León.
1032: Sancho extends his authority into Gascony.
1033: Sancho is king 'from Zamora to the borders of Barcelona'.
1034: León falls and Sancho is crowned again.
1035: Sancho III divides his realm among his four sons.
1035: Ferdinand takes Castile and the Pisuerga-Cea.
1035: the western conquests (León, Zamora, Salamanca) leave the kingdom.
1035: the Gascon protectorate lapses with Sancho's death.
1035: Gonzalo takes Sobrarbe and Ribagorza.
1035: Ramiro gets lands in Aragon.
1035: Gonzalo holds Sobrarbe and Ribagorza 'as vassal of his eldest brother, García'.
1045: Gonzalo dies and Ramiro absorbs Ribagorza.
1045: Calahorra is wrested from the Moors.
1054: Atapuerca.
1076: Alfonso VI takes La Rioja, Biscay, Álava, Durango and part of Gipuzkoa.
1076: Sancho Ramírez takes the rest.
1076: the Kingdom of Pamplona is partitioned between Castile and Aragon.

wars.name: Rebellion of Íñigo Arista with Musa ibn Musa
wars.outcome: 'In 841, in concert with Musa ibn Musa, Íñigo rebelled' (Navarre page); the Banu Qasi page has Abd ar-Rahman II defeat them and take Musa's son Lubb hostage.

wars.name: Battle of Albelda (Monte Laturce)
wars.outcome: 'In 859, Ordoño I of Asturias and García Íñiguez of Pamplona joined forces to deal Musa a crushing defeat.'

wars.name: Cordoban campaigns of 920 and 924 against Pamplona
wars.outcome: Abd al-Rahman III beat Navarre and León at Valdejunquera on 26 July 920 and sacked Pamplona; in 924 he devastated Basque territory in a counter-offensive against Sancho Ordóñez of Navarre.

wars.name: War of the Caliphate of Córdoba against Pamplona
wars.outcome: 'Clashes between the Caliphate of Córdoba and the kingdom resulted in the loss of Calahorra and the valley of the River Cidacos' (966).

wars.name: Conquests of Sancho III
wars.outcome: Sobrarbe (1015), Ribagorza (1018, 1025), Castile (1028; 1027 on the Sancho III page), the Pisuerga-Cea (1028 or 1030), Zamora (March 1033) and León (1034); at his death in 1035 'the kingdom had reached its greatest historical extent'.

wars.name: Battle of Atapuerca
wars.outcome: Ferdinand of Castile 'took from Pamplona the lands in La Bureba and the Tirón River'; García Sánchez III is killed.

wars.name: Partition of Pamplona after the murder of Sancho IV
wars.outcome: Alfonso VI of León and Castile takes La Rioja, Biscay, Álava, Durango and part of Gipuzkoa; Sancho Ramírez of Aragon takes the rest.

certainty.note: The pages give no boundary lines.
